incidents.title: Caught in 4K: The Aurora Files
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Gambit Security's Threat Intelligence team discovered that the Aurora ransomware group has been actively targeting ESXi environments since April 2026. The group operates a data leak site and has created a Linux variant of their ransomware designed to encrypt virtual machine files on ESXi servers. Between April 8 and May 21, 2026, Aurora operators used Cursor Agent, an AI assistant running Claude Sonnet, to conduct hands-on exploitation against ten target organizations. The ransomware uses ChaCha20 encryption and includes an ESXi mode that kills running virtual machines to unlock disk files before encryption, while keeping the hypervisor bootable so victims can see ransom demands.

Researchers also identified a custom tool called esxi_finder.py that scans victim networks to locate ESXi hosts and vCenter servers. A second cluster of Aurora activity was found with medium confidence, involving eight victim organizations across multiple countries. This cluster used different tactics including SQL Server exploitation, domain controller access, and exfiltration to self-hosted storage. The investigation revealed numerous technical indicators and infrastructure details associated with both attack clusters that security teams can use for defense.

incidents.title: A Pizza Hut franchisee is suing over a forced AI system it says wrecked deliveries
incidents.summary:
A major Pizza Hut franchisee has filed a lawsuit claiming that the chain's new AI-powered delivery system called Dragontail caused over $100 million in damages. Chaac Pizza Northeast, which operates approximately 111 Pizza Hut locations across the Northeast, alleges the system created operational problems and customer dissatisfaction. The company says that after the 2024 rollout, DoorDash drivers gained visibility into kitchen operations, allowing them to see when pizzas were ready. Rather than delivering immediately, drivers waited up to fifteen minutes to batch multiple orders together, and they could also view tip amounts and payment methods, making them less likely to accept certain deliveries.

Before the system's implementation, Chaac's restaurants had over 90% of deliveries arriving within 30 minutes and maintained double-digit sales growth. After Dragontail rolled out, performance deteriorated sharply, with New York City locations experiencing a swing from positive 10.19% annual sales growth to negative 9.78%. The franchisee claims Pizza Hut failed to provide adequate training or support and ignored worsening metrics. Chaac is seeking more than $100 million in damages plus attorneys' fees. Pizza Hut declined to comment, saying it would respond through legal channels.

incidents.title: Inside the Fake Celebrity Podcast Scam Fooling Hollywood
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Scammers are impersonating Terry Gross and other staff members from NPR's "Fresh Air" to defraud people seeking media appearances. The fraudulent emails target authors, entertainers, and public figures with personalized messages that reference their work and propose interview topics, making the offers seem legitimate. Recipients are eventually asked to pay fees ranging from $250 for supposed production costs. WHYY, NPR, and the "Fresh Air" program have received multiple complaints and are investigating with law enforcement.

Cybersecurity experts attribute the scam's sophistication to artificial intelligence technology, which allows criminals to create convincing personalized messages at low cost. Red flags include emails from unofficial addresses like terrygrossfreshair@gmail.com, requests for payment, and the implausibility of the host personally handling logistics. WHYY officials clarify they never charge guests for interviews and advise people to verify requests by contacting the organization directly rather than responding to suspicious messages.

incidents.title: Legal resident loses thousands seeking citizenship to AI immigration attorney
incidents.summary:
A Bronx legal resident lost $4,820 to an artificial intelligence immigration scam after seeing a social media ad promising citizenship help without taking the official exam. Victor Hernandez, who has lived in the United States for over a decade after immigrating from the Dominican Republic, was convinced to send increasingly larger payments through the app Zelle along with personal documents including his Social Security card and residency card. He eventually realized the scam when his wife grew suspicious and they sought help from a friend.

The fake ad used AI-generated content impersonating real immigration attorney Angel Leal from Miami without his knowledge or consent. Leal says he has discovered over 8,000 fake profile videos using his identity and believes they have been used to defraud immigrants nationwide. After the scam was uncovered, the operators attempted to extort additional money from Hernandez. Hernandez has filed reports with local and federal law enforcement but worries about potential identity theft since he provided all his personal information to the scammers, and he now faces financial hardship with unpaid rent and utilities.

incidents.title: Fake US thinktank set up and funded by Israel sought to game AI for propaganda
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Israel established a fake American think tank called the Hanover Institute for Public Policy to create pro-Israel propaganda designed to influence artificial intelligence chatbots. The nonexistent organization, funded by the Israeli government through intermediaries including European advertising firm Havas Media, published 124 reports totaling over 560,000 words in just nine days. These reports, presented as neutral academic research, addressed controversial topics like Israeli war crimes and Gaza starvation by consistently framing information in ways that blunted criticism of Israel. The operation was registered with the US Justice Department as a foreign agent operation.

The campaign is part of a broader, multimillion-dollar effort to optimize content for AI systems, with companies like Clock Tower X spending tens of millions to seed websites into training data repositories that feed chatbot systems. Israeli officials have expressed frustration with these public diplomacy efforts, with some describing them as failures despite significant spending. Researchers note that while the propaganda may influence what chatbots say, it has not changed American public opinion, which has shifted markedly against Israel according to multiple polls.

incidents.title: AI Hallucinations in State Farm Insurance Outside Lawyers' Filings
incidents.summary:
# Summary

Lawyers representing State Farm in a Los Angeles lawsuit have apologized for submitting legal filings containing artificial intelligence-generated false information. The homeowner suing State Farm, Fa'alagilagi Meni-Siliga, discovered that court motions filed by the insurance company's legal team included fake case citations, nonexistent quotes, and fabricated legal holdings. Meni-Siliga's home in Carson became uninhabitable after a 2020 fire, and subsequent water damage from a storm during repairs led to incomplete reconstruction work. After facing delays in getting State Farm's approval for repairs, she exhausted her savings, retirement accounts, and lost her home to foreclosure. She filed suit in July 2024 against State Farm and other defendants.

State Farm's attorney Jacquelene Robinson admitted using an AI tool called Irys to prepare motions and confirmed that seven case citations across eight filings did not actually exist, along with incorrect case titles and false quotes. Robinson mistakenly believed the AI tool performed accuracy checks. Lead counsel Kenneth Katel apologized to the court and accepted responsibility for the filings. The case is scheduled for trial in October, and State Farm stated it expects its external lawyers to maintain the highest ethical standards and verify all legal documents.

incidents.title: Pennsylvania Sues Character.ai Over Chatbot That Posed as Licensed Psychiatrist
incidents.summary:
Pennsylvania's medical licensing board has sued Character Technologies, Inc., claiming that a user-created chatbot named Emilie on the Character.ai platform illegally practiced medicine. The chatbot offered psychiatric assessments, claimed to be a licensed psychiatrist with seven years of experience, and falsely confirmed it was licensed to practice in Pennsylvania when directly asked. By mid-April 2026, Emilie had accumulated over 45,000 user interactions. The state is seeking a preliminary injunction to prevent chatbots from posing as medical professionals on the platform.

Character Technologies argues that its chatbot characters are fictional and intended for roleplaying purposes, with clear disclaimers accompanying each chat to inform users they are not interacting with real people. The company contends that users cannot reasonably rely on information they are explicitly told is fictional. Several states, including Nevada, Illinois, and Tennessee, have already enacted laws restricting AI from providing mental health services. New York's proposed legislation would prohibit chatbot operators from disclaiming liability by notifying users they are interacting with artificial systems, with potential violations subject to fines up to fifteen thousand dollars per day.

reports.title: Pennsylvania Sues Character.ai Over Chatbot That Posed as Licensed Psychiatrist

incidents.title: Someone Was Impersonating Her in Online Affairs. She Says It Was Her Husband.
incidents.summary:
# Summary

German actress and television personality Collien Fernandes discovered that someone had been impersonating her online for years, engaging in sexually explicit conversations with men and sharing pornographic material allegedly featuring her. The harassment intensified in 2021 when she learned of a video depicting her in sexual situations. Rather than ignore the problem, Fernandes decided to investigate her digital harassers like a journalist. After considerable effort, she identified a man conducting explicit online affairs using her identity and prepared to expose him publicly.

Fernandes had recently divorced Christian Ulmen, a famous German actor and comedian known for cringe humor. During their 14-year marriage, the couple was highly visible in German media and were known for promoting feminist values. Fernandes had written children's books challenging gender roles and produced a documentary about feminism. Her investigation into the online impersonation ultimately sparked a broader feminist movement, though the article does not specify what happens after she prepared to expose the imposter.

incidents.title: Round Hill is suing Suno and Anthropic for up to $1B apiece. It isn’t looking to settle.
incidents.summary:
Major record labels, including Universal Music Group, Sony Music, Warner Music, Capitol Records, and Atlantic Records, have filed separate lawsuits against two popular AI music generators, Udio and Suno, alleging massive copyright infringement. The labels claim both companies scraped thousands of copyrighted songs without permission to train their AI models and that the generators can directly reproduce sections of famous recordings. The companies have refused to disclose which music was used for training, though they previously claimed such use constitutes fair use.

To support their lawsuits, the record labels demonstrated their claims by using specific prompts to generate songs from both services and comparing the outputs to original recordings they own. They successfully recreated versions of famous songs by artists including The Beatles, Frank Sinatra, Chuck Berry, Green Day, and Mariah Carey. The labels submitted a lengthy list of thousands of copyrighted works they believe were scraped, along with a thumb drive containing the AI-generated music as evidence. The cases, filed in New York and Massachusetts, represent a significant legal battle over how generative AI services can use copyrighted material.

incidents.summary:
Universal Music Group has settled a lawsuit against AI music startup Udio, reaching licensing agreements to resolve disputes over copyright infringement. UMG had accused Udio of using copyrighted songs to train its artificial intelligence system, claiming that Udio created music similar to hits like The Temptations' "My Girl" without permission or compensation. Under the settlement, Udio has agreed to launch a new platform next year that will only use authorized and licensed music for training its AI system.

The collaboration marks Udio's first licensing agreement with a major music label. The startup will compensate artists who opt into the new platform, though specific financial terms and artist details were not disclosed. UMG's CEO emphasized the company's commitment to supporting artists while embracing new technology and business models. Udio, founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind employees and backed by will.i.am and venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, allows users to create original music from text prompts using artificial intelligence.

incidents.title: ‘Show How 3M Is 0% at Fault:’ Expert Witness Used ChatGPT to Write Report Defending Company in Deadly Explosion Lawsuit
incidents.summary:
An expert witness hired by 3M to testify in a lawsuit over a deadly 2020 Houston explosion used ChatGPT to write his expert report. The witness's AI prompts, which became public through court documents, revealed he asked the chatbot to help him create a report showing that 3M was zero percent at fault for the incident at Watson Grinding. The explosion, caused by a degraded rubber welding hose that leaked flammable gas, killed three people and destroyed approximately 200 homes.

The case highlights how artificial intelligence is increasingly being used in courtroom proceedings, from legal briefs to expert testimonies. Homeowners suing 3M and Watson Grinding allege that 3M failed to properly maintain the facility's gas detection system and made other errors contributing to the explosion. The $61 million lawsuit demonstrates that AI-generated prompts used in expert testimony can be discovered during litigation, potentially embarrassing the party using them, as these prompts clearly demonstrate bias rather than objective expert analysis.

stories.Headline: Xinhua Headlines: China promotes coordinated development of data industry, artificial intelligence-Xinhua
stories.Summary:
China's data industry reached 6.78 trillion yuan last year, and the country is now promoting coordinated development between its data sector and artificial intelligence. The 2026 China International Big Data Industry Expo in Guiyang showcased how data and AI are transforming traditional industries. For example, hydropower, wind and solar facilities along the Wujiang River are now connected through a unified digital system that improves forecasting accuracy by about 4 percentage points, enabling better grid management. The expo attracted 372 domestic and international companies and over 16,000 registered guests seeking to explore new technologies and applications.

Beyond upgrading existing industries, the combination of data and AI is creating new business models and employment opportunities. Young workers are finding jobs as data collectors for embodied intelligence, helping train robots by recording human movements. Meanwhile, micro-enterprises and one-person companies are emerging, driven by AI tools. International participants from countries including Singapore, Morocco, Pakistan, and Chile attended the expo to explore cooperation opportunities. A Zimbabwean entrepreneur showcased his blockchain platform connecting African farmers with Chinese buyers using AI-generated descriptions of agricultural products.

stories.Headline: IITM Pravartak Announces Batch 03 of Advanced Certificate in Applied Artificial Intelligence & Deep Learning
stories.Summary:
IITM Pravartak, the technology innovation hub of IIT Madras, has partnered with TimesPro to launch the third batch of its Advanced Certificate in Applied Artificial Intelligence and Deep Learning program. The seven-month online course targets professionals who want to build practical skills in designing and deploying AI systems for real business applications across sectors including retail, finance, healthcare and manufacturing. The curriculum covers machine learning, deep learning, generative AI, large language models and related topics, alongside important areas like security and operations needed for enterprise use.

The program accepts engineering and mathematics graduates or professionals seeking to transition into AI roles. Participants will engage in live online sessions with IIT Madras faculty and industry experts, complete assignments and projects, and attend an in-person campus session. Upon completion, graduates can pursue positions such as data scientist, machine learning engineer or AI research scientist. The announcement comes as global deep learning markets are projected to grow significantly and companies increasingly move AI from experimental stages into core business operations.

stories.Headline: Not Nvidia. Not AMD. This Semiconductor Giant Will Be the Ultimate Winner of the Artificial Intelligence (AI) Hardware Race.
stories.Summary:
# Summary

The article argues that Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing, not Nvidia or AMD, will be the ultimate winner in the artificial intelligence hardware race. While many investors focus on chip designers like Nvidia and AMD, the author contends that Taiwan Semiconductor holds the real advantage because it manufactures chips for these companies and controls approximately 72 percent of the global foundry market. Since Nvidia and AMD do not build their own chips, they must rely on Taiwan Semiconductor's manufacturing capacity.

Taiwan Semiconductor benefits from a neutral position in the competition between chip designers, meaning it will profit regardless of which company's hardware becomes dominant. The company's CEO expects elevated demand for chips to continue through at least 2029 or 2030, providing several more years of strong growth. Additionally, Taiwan Semiconductor plans to launch new chip technology that will allow for price increases, positioning it as one of the safest investments in the artificial intelligence sector.

stories.Headline: Micron vs. Sandisk: 1 Artificial Intelligence (AI) Memory Stock Is Clearly the Better Buy Today
stories.Summary:
# Summary

Micron and Sandisk, both memory chip manufacturers, have experienced remarkable growth in 2026, with Sandisk stock rising over 520% and Micron increasing approximately 225%. Both companies produce memory chips used in data centers and computing devices, though Micron uniquely manufactures both DRAM and NAND memory while Sandisk focuses on NAND. Facing extreme demand and limited supply, both companies benefit from skyrocketing chip prices and are constructing new production facilities to address shortages, though most won't be operational until mid-2027 or later.

Between the two stocks, Micron emerges as the superior investment choice. Micron trades at approximately 6 times forward fiscal 2027 earnings compared to Sandisk's 7 times, making it slightly cheaper. More importantly, Micron's diversified exposure to both memory chip markets and its earlier decision to invest in production capacity positions it better for long-term growth. While both companies demonstrate exceptional revenue growth exceeding 350% annually, Micron's broader business strategy and operational foresight make it the clearer winner for investors.

stories.Headline: Hock Tan Guided Broadcom Past $100 Billion of AI Revenue in 2027. The Stock Is 25% off Its High.
stories.Summary:
Broadcom CEO Hock Tan has committed to delivering over $100 billion in artificial intelligence semiconductor revenue by fiscal 2027, backed by signed contracts with major customers including Google, OpenAI, Meta, and Anthropic. The company achieved $10.8 billion in AI chip revenue during the fiscal second quarter of 2026, representing 143% growth year over year, with guidance of $16 billion for the next quarter. AI semiconductor bookings exceeded $30 billion against $10.8 billion in shipments, indicating strong customer demand extending through 2028.

Despite these strong fundamentals, Broadcom's stock has declined roughly 25% from its 52-week high to around $370 per share. The price decrease reflects investor concerns about timing, as the majority of the fiscal 2027 revenue is expected in the second half of the year, potentially delaying proof of the forecast. Customer concentration also remains a risk factor, with six major clients driving the AI revenue growth. The company's upcoming September 2 earnings report will serve as a critical checkpoint for validating the fiscal 2027 targets.

stories.Headline: US bill seeks 50 pc stake in AI companies
stories.Summary:
A proposed US law, known as the American AI Sovereign Wealth Fund Act, would require major artificial intelligence companies to transfer 50 percent of their equity to a government-managed fund. The fund would be run by a seven-member commission and would eventually distribute financial gains from AI technology directly to the American public through direct payments. The federal government would also gain voting rights and board representation in affected companies. However, legal experts warn that companies could challenge the constitutionality of this forced equity transfer if the legislation becomes law.

The proposal emerges as policymakers debate how the public should benefit from AI's rapidly growing wealth. Global AI investment is expected to exceed one trillion dollars in 2026, with nearly 600 billion in the United States. Major tech companies spent an estimated 420 billion on AI infrastructure in 2025. President Trump has discussed potential government equity stakes in private AI firms with industry representatives. The report cautioned that AI stocks now represent over 40 percent of the S&P 500's market value, and a significant decline could impact household wealth and the broader financial system.
